name: TRIP C - the surcharge case (LON->MRY, plus a same-metal comparison)
description: C1 is Trip B's real LON->MRY leg, scored with the surcharge model. C2 is a constructed business-cabin leg that exercises the same-metal alternatives engine, which C1's economy cabin cannot.
source: C1 transcribes the real LON->MRY capture (Google Flights, 2026-09-07, Tsuki). C2 is CONSTRUCTED for acceptance testing and is NOT a real captured itinerary - its award prices are labelled synthetic and must never be quoted as real.
trip_level_flags: C2 IS SYNTHETIC. Its points prices are invented for the purpose of exercising the alternatives engine and are labelled as such on every candidate. C1 is real captured data.

C1's British Airways option carries a carrier-imposed surcharge that was NOT captured. Scoring it as $0 would show a saving of roughly $282 that does not exist. The surcharge is modelled as a range, never as zero.

legs.description: LON->MRY, Jan 27 2027, one-way, economy, 1 adult (real capture; arrives SFO)
notes: This is Trip B's B4 leg, isolated so the surcharge behaviour can be pinned by a test.
Departing LHR is the worst case in the surcharge model: UK Air Passenger Duty stacks on top of the carrier-imposed surcharge.
data_flags: NO option actually arrives MRY. All arrive SFO. Return positioning SFO->Monterey is unpriced.
The economy surcharge for British Airways ex-LHR is NOT in the model. The research behind data/surcharges.csv is business-cabin only, and economy figures were deliberately not extrapolated from it.

points_candidates.label: British Airways LHR-SFO nonstop (badge 20k pts)
points_candidates.source_note: Google Flights '20k pts' badge. UNVERIFIED. BA awards DEPARTING LHR carry UK Air Passenger Duty plus BA carrier-imposed surcharges. That figure was NOT captured, and v1 refuses to model it: the seed table is business-cabin and this is economy.

points_candidates.label: United LHR-SFO nonstop (badge 27.6k pts)
points_candidates.source_note: Google Flights '27.6k pts' badge. UNVERIFIED. United levies no carrier-imposed surcharge as a matter of program policy, which is why this resolves to a confirmed $0. UK departure taxes are still owed and are NOT modelled.

legs.description: SYNTHETIC: JFK->DUB, business, on Aer Lingus metal, priced in British Airways Executive Club
notes: CONSTRUCTED CASE, not a capture. It exists to exercise alternatives.find_same_metal_alternatives(): the same EI aeroplane can be ticketed in Aer Lingus AerClub, whose surcharge band IS modelled, while BA Executive Club's surcharge on EI metal is not.
data_flags: SYNTHETIC POINTS PRICE. 50,000 Avios is invented for this test and is not a real award price.
